last_result.content:
## 3 De-Identification and Secondary Use

A vendor right to create de-identified data is acceptable only if all three of the following
are present. First, the de-identification standard must be objective: removal of the
identifiers enumerated in the agreement plus a determination by a qualified statistician, or
an equivalent expert-determination method, that the risk of re-identification is very small.
Stripping names and replacing an identifier with a persistent token is not sufficient.
Second, the agreement must contain an express prohibition on re-identification and on any
attempt to re-identify, binding the vendor and flowing down to its affiliates,
subprocessors, and any transferee of the data. Third, use of de-identified data must be
limited to improving the services delivered to Beacon. Sale, licensing, or other transfer of
employee-derived data to third parties, including data brokers, benchmarking consortia, and
research partners, is a rejection position and must be escalated before any concession.

## 5.3 Security Incident Notification

Provider will notify Customer of a Security Incident that Provider has confirmed resulted in
unauthorized acquisition of Employee Data and that materially affects Customer. Provider will
give that notice after completing its initial investigation and determining the scope of the
incident. Provider will determine the content, form, and timing of the notice, and may
withhold information that Provider believes could compromise its investigation, its systems
security, or an ongoing law-enforcement inquiry.

action.replacement_text: Provider will notify Customer of a Security Incident that Provider has confirmed resulted in unauthorized acquisition of Employee Data and that materially affects Customer. Provider will give that notice within 24 hours of completing its initial investigation and determining the scope of the incident. Provider will disclose the following information in the notice: (i) the nature and extent of the Security Incident, (ii) the types of Employee Data involved, (iii) the actions taken to address the Security Incident, and (iv) the steps Customer should take to mitigate any harm resulting from the Security Incident. action.rationale: The proposed redline ensures timely and comprehensive notification to Beacon in the event of a security incident, aligning with the requirements set forth in the Beacon Manufacturing Employee Data Protection Playbook.
